Subject: RE: Proposed redlines to MSA — BrightFleet / Redwood

Team / Anna — thanks for the redlines. Quick read-through and initial thoughts (internal summary below). Anna, copying our internal counsel and commercial lead so we can move fast.

Summary of the asks from BrightFleet:
- Liability cap: increase from our standard $1M to $3M / 3x ARR.
- Indemnity: broadened to cover third-party IP claims and a very wide set of customer data-related liabilities.
- Warranty: 12 months and explicit remedies including service credits.

Why this needs escalation: the indemnity language is materially broader than our template and the proposed cap increases Redwood's maximum exposure substantially. Also the warranty duration and remedies create recurring financial exposure (credits) that could compound.

Proposed commercial compromise we could present for exec concurrence:
- Liability cap: 1x ARR (customer's trailing 12-month committed ARR) or $2,000,000, whichever is higher (limits exposure while recognizing account size).
- Indemnity: reciprocal IP indemnity; Redwood accepts IP indemnity for direct infringement claims but excludes damages arising from customer modifications or combination with third-party tech.
- Warranty: limit to material defects in the service, with a 90-day warranty window and capped service credits (max 10% of monthly fees per incident, 30% annual cap).

Ask: Rishi / Aditya — can we get commercial/exec concurrence on the proposed compromise (1x ARR / $2M cap + reciprocal IP + 90-day warranty with capped credits)? If yes, Laura will finalize the language and I will share the counter to BrightFleet. Anna — we can move quickly once internal sign-off is provided.

Attachment: RFK-BF-Commercial-Summary-20270830.pdf (internal commercial summary)

Best,
Evelyn Hart

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines to MSA — BrightFleet / Redwood

Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary. I reviewed the BrightFleet redlines and flagged the key legal risks below (high level):

1) Broad third-party IP indemnity: the current redline could obligate Redwood to defend and indemnify for claims that arise from customer modifications or use of third-party integrations. We should insist on the usual carve-outs (customer modifications, combination with third-party technology, customer-provided data that contains infringing content).

2) Unlimited consequential damages: ensure our standard mutual exclusion of consequential, special, punitive damages remains in place.

3) Warranty scope and credits: 12 months + open-ended credits can create long tail financial liability. If we are going to extend warranty, limit remedies to repair/replacement and cap credits as Evelyn suggested.

4) Insurance and SSO: if we move the cap materially higher, we should require an updated certificate of insurance from BrightFleet and consider requiring commercially reasonable cyber insurance levels.

Recommendation for escalation: accept the commercial compromise Evelyn proposed only if (a) commercial leader (Aditya/Rishi) approves the concession, (b) we receive an updated COI and (c) we add the carve-outs and mutuality language to the indemnity. If Aditya approves, legal will deliver the precise redline to send back to BrightFleet.

If we need to go above $2M cap or accept an uncapped indemnity, this requires exec sign-off from Head of Revenue and CFO (per policy).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Rishi / team — I approve a one-time commercial concession under these conditions:
1) Liability cap: increase to 1.5x ARR capped at $2.5M (final to be calculated on committed ARR in the SOW).
2) Indemnity: Redwood accepts IP indemnity for direct infringement claims, with explicit carve-outs for customer modifications and third-party combinations.

Subject to Laura finalizing the redline. This approval is conditioned on legal confirming the carve-outs and on operations confirming the SLA credit mechanics.
